name: DSTDEV
description: DSTDEV estimates the standard deviation of the numeric values in a specified field of the database records that match the given criteria, treating the matching records as a sample of a population.
tldr: Sample standard deviation of a database column for rows that meet the criteria.

parameters.name: database
parameters.description: The range containing the database, including the header row as the first row.

parameters.name: field
parameters.description: The column to analyze, given as the column label in quotes (e.g. "Yield") or its 1-based column index.

parameters.name: criteria
parameters.description: The range with a header row matching database column names and one or more condition rows; only matching records are analyzed.

basicExample.description: Sample standard deviation of Yield for apple trees taller than 10
basicExample.explanation: The two matching rows have Yield 14 and 10. The mean is 12, squared deviations are 4 and 4 (sum 8), divided by n-1 = 1 gives 8, and the square root is about 2.828.

advancedExamples.title: Compare with population version
advancedExamples.description: DSTDEVP divides by n instead of n-1, giving a smaller value for the same two points.
advancedExamples.explanation: With n=2, the population variance is 8/2 = 4, so the standard deviation is 2, versus the sample 2.828.

advancedExamples.title: Wider sample of all apple trees
advancedExamples.description: Compute the sample standard deviation over three apple yields.
advancedExamples.explanation: Apple yields 14, 10, 6 have mean 10; squared deviations 16, 0, 16 sum to 32; divided by 2 gives variance 16; sqrt is 4.

howItWorks: DSTDEV filters the database to rows matching the criteria, then computes the sample standard deviation of the numeric values in the specified field: it takes the square root of the sample variance, where the sum of squared deviations from the mean is divided by n-1 (the number of matching records minus one). Use DSTDEV when the matching records are a sample, not the whole population.

howToSteps.name: Set up the database
howToSteps.text: Enter your table with a header row, e.g. A1:E7 with Tree, Height, Age, Yield, Profit.

howToSteps.name: Set up criteria
howToSteps.text: Place criteria headers and values in a separate range, e.g. A9:B10.

limitations: Assumes the matching records are a sample; use DSTDEVP for an entire population.
Needs at least two matching numeric values, or the result is undefined (#DIV/0! when n is less than 2).
Criteria header labels must exactly match database headers.

commonErrors.cause: Fewer than two records matched, so the sample (n-1) denominator is zero or negative.
commonErrors.fix: Ensure the criteria match at least two records, or use a different statistic for single values.

commonErrors.cause: The field was an unquoted column name.
commonErrors.fix: Wrap the field name in quotes, e.g. "Yield", or use the column index.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: DSTDEV works identically in Google Sheets with the same arguments and behavior.

faq.question: When should I use DSTDEV instead of DSTDEVP?
faq.answer: Use DSTDEV when the matching rows are a sample of a larger population; use DSTDEVP when they represent the whole population.

faq.question: Why is my DSTDEV result larger than DSTDEVP?
faq.answer: DSTDEV divides by n-1 while DSTDEVP divides by n, so the sample estimate is generally larger.

faq.question: What happens with only one matching row?
faq.answer: DSTDEV returns #DIV/0! because a sample needs at least two values.
